title: Centre tells Netflix to keep its first Pakistani series off Indian screens
dek: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry cited its May 2025 advisory against Pakistan-origin content after film workers' unions objected to the 4 December release of 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'. Netflix has not said whether India is in the release.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has asked Netflix to make sure that Pakistan-origin content, including its first Pakistani original series, is not streamed in India, according to reports citing unnamed officials. The series, the romantic drama Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, released internationally as All the Love Our Hearts Carry, is due to premiere on 4 December.

The ministry acted after receiving several complaints and representations about a possible Indian release, and told Netflix to follow its advisory of 8 May 2025, issued "in the interest of national security", according to reports. It also reminded the company of its commitment in June 2025 that no Pakistan-origin film or series was available to Indian subscribers. Netflix has not commented publicly and has not said whether India is among the markets for the release.

## What the 2025 advisory says

The advisory, numbered DM/9/2025-DM and signed by a deputy director in the ministry, is addressed to OTT platforms, media streaming platforms and intermediaries. It cites the code of ethics for online publishers under the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, which tells them to exercise "due caution and discretion" over content that affects India's sovereignty, threatens the security of the State or harms "India's friendly relations with foreign countries". It refers to the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025 and says: "In the interest of national security, all OTT platforms, media streaming platforms and intermediaries operating in India are advised to discontinue the web-series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media content, whether made available on a subscription based model or otherwise, having its origins in Pakistan with immediate effect."

The advisory is not a law passed by Parliament, but platforms that ignore it risk action under the 2021 rules, which set up a three-tier grievance system ending with an inter-departmental committee of the ministry.

## Who objected

The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India on 24 November, saying a release would go against the spirit of the advisory. The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE), an umbrella body of 32 associations which says it has five lakh members, wrote a day later backing that request. Its president, B N Tiwari, said: "For us, the country comes first, and Pakistani artists are not welcome." FWICE warned it would stop shoots of all Netflix projects if the series is released in India, and restated its policy that members should not work with Pakistani artists or technicians in film, television, web or music, according to reports.

In Pakistan, Planning and Development Minister Ahsan Iqbal accused India of "weaponising sports, then water, and now art and culture", according to reports.

## The series

Directed and produced by Momina Duraid, the series adapts Farhat Ishtiaq's 2013 Urdu novel. Its cast includes Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan, both of whom have worked in Hindi films, along with Sanam Saeed, Ahad Raza Mir, Iqra Aziz, Hania Aamir and Hamza Ali Abbasi. Pakistani television dramas built a large following in India through streaming before 2025, and Fawad Khan's Hindi film Abir Gulaal was kept from release in India after the Pahalgam attack.

## Background

Relations between the two countries have been at their lowest in years since the April 2025 attack, which was followed by Indian strikes on Pakistan in May 2025, the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty and curbs on trade and travel. The streaming advisory was one of a series of measures that also included blocking Pakistani YouTube channels and social media accounts in India.

## What happens next

The series is due on 4 December. Whether Netflix withholds it in India or geo-blocks it will be the first test of the 2025 advisory against a major global platform's own production.
